name: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6

lineage.base_model: PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 (compatible); ERNIE4.5 tag on the card

purpose: Compact document parsing: pages to structured output including text, tables, formulas, charts and seals, plus text spotting. Distributed through the PaddleOCR toolkit, which adds page-level layout parsing. The 1.6 report (arXiv 2606.03264) names under-optimised region refinement and progressive post-training as the focus (title only; paper not read).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: LICENSE file of the model repo is the unmodified Apache License 2.0 text (read 2026-11-19); card tag agrees

variants.notes: model file 0.94 GB plus mmproj 0.88 GB (HF tree sizes; precision of the files not stated on the card tree); created 2026-05-29, 104,439 downloads

engine_support.notes: llama.cpp support merged 2026-02-19 (PR 18825, mtmd, needs mmproj); an official 1.6 GGUF repo now exists; spotting needs a metadata change on the mmproj (image_max_pixels 1605632); the GGUF path covers recognition only, layout needs PaddlePaddle

benchmarks.name: MORE German overall (per-language, 149 languages)
benchmarks.harness: read through a summarizer; MORE overall 87.96 over 149 languages, table 61.11, code 96.29

strengths: German is one of its stronger languages in third-party tests (MDPBench DE 84.1-84.8, among the top specialised open models)
weaknesses: page-level parsing needs the PaddleOCR pipeline, the bare model does element-level recognition
GGUF path needs two files and special prompts
independent MDPBench puts 1.6 below 1.5 overall (75.0 vs 78.3) while the vendor OmniDocBench number rises: vendor numbers and a third-party multilingual/photo benchmark disagree
best_for: bulk PDF/scan parsing to Markdown on a small GPU or CPU
soft.maturity: Baidu PaddlePaddle ecosystem, regular releases (1.0 to 1.6 within about a year); large community

user_reports.summary: guide on the 1.0 llama.cpp merge: Stage 2 (recognition) only, layout stage still needs PaddlePaddle, chat template crashes without --jinja in the first builds; one author reports accurate English and several European languages including German in an informal check

tona_fit.reason: best-evidenced small page parser for German: third-party German scores 84.1 (1.6) and 84.8 (1.5), Apache-2.0 verified, 0.9B, official GGUF; Tona lacking an OCR module is only a blocker, not a quality issue. Choose between 1.5 and 1.6 on our own German pages (MDPBench prefers 1.5, the vendor benchmark 1.6).
blockers: Tona engine has no vision/OCR architecture; would run through llama.cpp
